theater: 多瑙河中游盆地與涅達奧河谷

battle.name: 日耳曼-匈人戰爭
battle.theater: 多瑙河中游盆地與涅達奧河谷
battle.brief: 阿提拉於公元四五三年死後，匈人帝國的西翼崩解，蓋皮德人國王阿爾達里克聯合其他日耳曼部族起兵，在涅達奧河畔擊潰匈王埃拉克的騎兵大軍，匈人西進之路自此截斷。卡面的亞述長矛出自九百年前，並未出現在這場戰鬥；它真正的作用是那種插柄鐵矛頭的祖型，五世紀的日耳曼長矛仍沿著這條工藝傳統走下去。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 日耳曼-匈人戰爭，即涅達奧之戰，是公元四五四年阿提拉死後爆發的一場決戰，交戰雙方是草原帝國匈人與多瑙河中游的日耳曼聯盟。匈人方面是阿提拉留下的帝國殘部：長子埃拉克率領匈牙利平原與東歐草原的核心部眾，弟弟登吉奇、厄爾格、烏爾丁各自控制一片帳幕王國；帝國的骨架是匈奴王公對被征服的日耳曼與羅馬屬部所維持的宗主關係，匈人兵源裡大量是哥特人、蓋皮德人、舒易比人等被征服民族的青壯。蓋皮德一方由國王阿爾達里克率領，聯盟裡還有哥特人、舒易比人與其他受匈人管制的部族，戰後阿爾達里克被這些部族推為共主。這個聯盟既不是羅馬的行省也不是羅馬的軍團，而是以王權、盟誓與戰利品瓜分維繫的部落聯盟，靠自己的步兵與弓手作戰，羅馬軍隊並未參戰。真正把雙方拉到對面的是共同的敵意：匈人帝國要求屬部提供兵員、馬匹與貢賦，而阿爾達里克的蓋皮德人原本被阿提拉安置在多瑙河與蒂薩河一帶充當帝國的北翼屏障，如今要趁主子新亡取回自由。戰後的格局同樣牽動羅馬：東羅馬皇帝利奧一世在四五五年致信阿爾達里克，請求蓋皮德人出兵攻打匈人，這封信是日耳曼人頭一次以對等盟友的身分被羅馬皇帝單獨致書。
countriesEn: The Germanic-Hunnic War, that is, the Battle of Nedao, was a decisive battle fought in AD 454 after the death of Attila, between the steppe empire of the Huns and a Germanic alliance in the middle Danube. On the Hunnic side stood the remnant of Attila's empire: the eldest son Ellac led the core peoples of the Hungarian plain and the east European steppe, while his brothers Dengizich, Erge and Uldin each controlled a separate tented realm; the framework of that empire was a lordship maintained by Hunnic princes over conquered Germanic and Roman subject peoples, and much of the manpower in the Huns' ranks was drawn from the young men of the Goths, Gepids, Suebi and other conquered peoples. The Gepid side was led by the king Ardaric, and the alliance also contained Goths, Suebi and other tribes under Hunnic control; after the victory Ardaric was acknowledged as their joint leader. This alliance was neither a Roman province nor a Roman legion but a tribal confederation held together by kingship, sworn alliance and the division of plunder, fought with its own infantry and archers, and no Roman troops took part. What genuinely set the two sides against each other was a common hatred: the Hunnic empire demanded men, horses and tribute from its subjects, and Ardaric's Gepids, whom Attila had settled along the Danube and the Tisza to serve as the northern shield of the empire, meant to take back their freedom now that their overlord had just died. The outcome also concerned Rome: in AD 455 the eastern emperor Leo I wrote to Ardaric asking the Gepids to attack the Huns, and that letter is the earliest record of a Germanic people being addressed as an equal ally by a Roman emperor.
people: 這場戰爭沒有留下羅馬將軍的名字，樞紐全在匈人王庭與蓋皮德王族兩處。阿提拉本人在四五三年死於蒂薩河畔的營帳，據約丹尼斯記載，他以鼻子出血為徵兆，死時娶的是哥特女子克雷卡。他的死留下三個問題：草原的兵歸誰、帝國的屬部是否繼續臣服、匈牙利平原與多瑙河中游的貢賦由誰收取。長子埃拉克承接汗位後選擇以刀兵維繫帝國，他先平定不服的屬部，隨後把矛頭指向蓋皮德人，這一舉動把整個日耳曼部族世界推成了聯盟。蓋皮德人的國王阿爾達里克是最終決定戰局的人：他手握蓋皮德王族的兵與土地，又握有其他部族願意追隨的正當性名分，於是成為聯軍的實際統帥。埃拉克在戰陣中被流矢射中面部而陣亡，此說出自約丹尼斯，並非戰記，匈人失去主將當場崩散，蓋皮德人趁勢追擊並奪取匈人的營帳與馬群。掌權的後繼者是阿爾達里克之子瓦達里克以及他的孫子歐根，瓦達里克在四五五年回覆利奧一世的信中陳述蓋皮德人的戰績，歐根則把帝國殘部整合進蓋皮德王國。關於本役的另一個重要人物是約丹尼斯本人：這位六世紀的史家是本役唯一的系統敘述者，他出身東哥特系，寫《匈人史》時明顯站在蓋皮德人一邊，把這場戰鬥描寫成日耳曼人復國的起點，因此他的記載既是本篇的主要依據，也必須帶著懷疑去讀。
peopleEn: No Roman general is named in this war; the whole hinge lies in the Hunnic court and in the Gepid royal house. Attila himself died in 453 in his camp on the banks of the Tisza; according to Jordanes he was taken by a nosebleed, and he was married at the time to the Gothic woman Kreka. His death left three questions open: who would command the steppe, whether the subject peoples would go on obeying, and who would collect the tribute of the Hungarian plain and the middle Danube. Ellac, the eldest son, took the khanate and chose to hold the empire together by force: he first crushed the disobedient subjects and then turned on the Gepids, and that single decision pushed the whole Germanic tribal world into a coalition. Ardaric, king of the Gepids, was the man who finally decided the battle: he held the soldiers and the land of the Gepid royal house, and he held the legitimacy that the other tribes were willing to follow, and so he became the effective commander of the coalition. Ellac was killed in the fighting, struck in the face by a stray arrow, a detail that comes from Jordanes and not from a battle report; the Huns broke up on the spot without a leader, and the Gepids pursued them and took their tents and their horses. Those who took over afterwards were Ardaric's son Vadaric and his grandson Aoric; Vadaric set out the Gepid war record in his reply to Leo I in 455, and Aoric folded the surviving parts of the empire into the Gepid kingdom. The other important figure for this battle is Jordanes himself: the sixth-century historian is the only systematic narrator of it, he came from an East Gothic family, and in his Getica he openly sides with the Gepids and presents the fight as the starting point of a Germanic restoration. His account is therefore the principal source for this dossier and at the same time something that has to be read with suspicion.
kits: 卡面是亞述長矛：一支約公元前九百年的短柄矛，鐵鏃套在木柄上，刃身狹長有中脊。它的戰史位置在這場戰役裡其實是對照件，不是實物。公元四五四年，多瑙河中游的日耳曼長矛早已不是亞述形制：矛頭更寬更扁，中脊更高，套筒口做出凸緣以便安在木柄上，考古上正是這種插柄式矛頭被當作第四至第六世紀的斷代標尺；匈人與蓋皮德人各自的矛頭在同一個歐亞大陸上並行，說明亞述人留下的不是樣式，而是插柄鐵矛頭這個工藝傳統本身。真正上陣的裝備要分兩邊寫。匈人一邊是全套遊牧騎兵的配備：複合反曲弓，骨、角、筋、木四層黏合，長度只到六十至七十公分，騎在馬上張弓，箭鏃是骨製或鐵製；短柄矛與長矛頭、鐵柄直刀與彎刀、匕首、札甲與皮札甲、蒙面小圓盾，後期才出現的馬鐙與鐵馬嚼，帳外營帳與畜群隨軍移動，車隊是真正的後勤主幹。日耳曼聯盟一邊是典型的民族遷移期步兵：長矛、鐵劍與長身劍、小型圓盾或橢圓形長盾，鎧甲以鎖子甲與札甲為主，貴族層級的裝飾件集中在金器上，羅馬尼亞彼得羅阿薩出土的蓋皮德王族寶藏裡有一枚金鷹形扣飾，上面刻著代表蓋皮德人自稱的銘文，是本役雙方身分的實物旁證。亞述人自己的裝備同樣有脈絡可循：短矛兵結密集橫列，前後以弓箭手與投石手支援，另有輕車與騎兵、攻城塔與撞槌，也就是說那支亞述長矛從來不是靠單兵發力取勝的兵器，它背後站著整套投射火力體系。
kitsEn: The card shows an Assyrian spear: a short-shafted spear of about 900 BC whose iron head fitted onto a wooden shaft, with a narrow long blade carrying a central rib. Its historical position in this battle is in fact that of a reference piece, not an actual object. In AD 454 the Germanic lances of the middle Danube were no longer Assyrian in shape: the heads were broader and flatter, with a stronger midrib, and the socket was fashioned with a collar so that it could be seated on the shaft; in archaeology it is precisely this socketed spearhead that serves as a dating marker for the fourth to sixth centuries. The Hunnic and Gepid spearheads run in parallel across the same Eurasian world, which shows that what the Assyrians handed down was not a style but the craft tradition of the socketed iron spearhead itself. The equipment that actually went into the fight has to be described side by side. On the Hunnic side it is the full kit of the nomadic horseman: the composite recurved bow of bone, horn, sinew and wood, only sixty to seventy centimetres long, shot from the saddle, with bone or iron arrowheads; barbed javelin and lance heads, straight swords with iron blades and sabres, daggers, lamellar and leather armour, small round shields faced with hide, and stirrups and iron bits appearing only late in the century, with tents and herds moving along with the army so that the wagon train was the real backbone of the logistics. The Germanic alliance fielded the standard infantry of the migration period: long spears, iron swords and spathae, small round or long oval shields, mail and lamellar armour, while the aristocratic layer shows up in goldwork, notably the eagle-shaped gold fibula from the Pietroasa treasure in Romania, which carries the inscription used by the Gepids as their own name and is material evidence for the identity of both sides in this battle. The Assyrian equipment has a lineage of its own: the spearmen stood in dense ranks, supported before and behind by archers and slingers, with light chariots and cavalry, siege towers and battering rams. In other words the Assyrian spear never won anything on its own; it stood behind an entire system of missile firepower.
tactics: 匈人的戰法寫在兩樣東西上：一是五世紀匈牙利出土銀碗上那列騎兵的畫面，十餘騎依次前進，馬上的人持弓；二是草原民族本身的騎射紀律。匈人通常不願在開闊地上跟人硬撞，愛好用密集騎兵反覆掠過敵陣前，傾瀉箭雨，逼對方亂陣，再拉開距離重複，最後才以長矛與馬刀衝鋒；遇到不利地形就退走，幾乎不留死屍給敵人收拾。埃拉克把這套打法帶到涅達奧河時遇上的是相反的條件：匈牙利西部多瑙河與蒂薩河之間是沼澤、柳林與河曲交錯的濕地，開闊平原被水與樹切碎，騎兵的衝鋒速度與射界同時被削平。蓋皮德人一邊走的是民族遷移期步兵的老路：盾牌結成密排，長矛從盾縫後方平舉，重步兵為骨幹，馬隊只用來掩護側翼與追擊。決定戰局的不是正面硬撞，而是三個瞬間：匈人主將埃拉克陣亡，士氣當場崩掉；聯軍利用林地與沼澤切斷了匈人撤退的通道；蓋皮德騎兵在追擊中奪走匈人的馬群與帳篷車隊。戰後匈人放棄多瑙河中游，向東退回黑海北岸草原，聯軍則接管了原屬匈人的多瑙河與蒂薩河流域。
tacticsEn: The way the Huns fought is written down in two things: the column of horsemen, some ten or more of them, shown on a fifth-century silver bowl found in Hungary; and the shooting discipline of the steppe peoples themselves. The Huns normally avoided crashing head-on with an enemy in the open. They preferred to sweep repeatedly in front of the opposing line with massed cavalry, pouring arrows on it, breaking its order, then drawing off and repeating, and only closing with lance and sabre for the final charge; given unfavourable ground they withdrew, leaving almost no dead for the enemy to collect. Ellac brought that doctrine to the Nedao and met the opposite conditions: the belt between the Danube and the Tisza in western Hungary is a country of marshes, willow scrub and meandering channels, where the open plain is broken up by water and trees, and the speed and the shooting arc of the cavalry are blunted at the same time. The Gepids followed the old path of the migration-period foot soldier: shields closed into a dense array, spears held level through the gaps, the heavy infantry forming the core, and the mounted men used only to cover the flanks and to pursue. What decided the battle was not the frontal collision but three moments: the death of the Hunnic commander Ellac, which broke their morale on the spot; the cutting of the Hunnic retreat by marsh and woodland; and the seizure of the Hunnic horse herds and wagon train during the pursuit. After the battle the Huns gave up the middle Danube and withdrew east to the steppe north of the Black Sea, while the alliance took over the Danube and Tisza valleys that had belonged to the Huns.
data: 先說年代：戰爭列表把本條的年份標為公元前四五三年，但同一條的中文條目所對應的英文名是涅達奧之戰，該役發生於公元四五四年，即阿提拉死後的翌年，兩者相差九百餘年，列表此處的年代應屬誤植，本篇按史實的公元四五四年記，月份亦無可靠記載，暫取四月。兵力方面，唯一的系統敘述者約丹尼斯完全沒有留下本役的兵員數字，只說匈人兵敗、埃拉克陣亡、匈軍四散；現代研究對五世紀匈人可調動的騎兵常以數萬量級估算，那是全體系國家的總量，不是本役的實數。蓋皮德聯盟的人數同樣無記載，考古上能對應的，是匈牙利西部第四、五世紀墓葬中大量出土的插柄式矛頭、札甲殘片與馬具。時間上，本役是一日定勝負的決戰；距離上，涅達奧河谷到多瑙河畔約一百五十至二百公里，阿爾達里克其後的蓋皮德王國就建立在蒂薩河與多瑙河之間，面積約十幾萬平方公里。可核對的相關年代還有：阿提拉在位四三四年至四五三年，利奧一世致阿爾達里克的信在四五五年，匈人在四六九年至四七〇年因登吉奇反叛被羅馬打敗，四七六年羅馬把一批匈人部眾安置在潘諾尼亞，四八七年奧多亞克攻滅留在多瑙河畔的魯吉人，蓋皮德王國則延續到五六年前後才被倫巴德人與阿伏爾人掃掉。
dataEn: First the dating: the list of wars marks this entry with the year 453 BC, but the Chinese name of the same entry corresponds in English to the Battle of Nedao, which was fought in AD 454, the year after Attila died; the two differ by more than nine centuries, so the date in the list is a misprint, and this dossier follows the historical year, AD 454. The month is not reliably recorded and is provisionally taken as April. On strength, the only systematic narrator, Jordanes, leaves no figure at all for the troops in this battle; he says only that the Huns were defeated, that Ellac was killed and that the Hunnic army dissolved. Modern estimates of the Hunnic cavalry that could be mobilised in the fifth century are commonly on the order of tens of thousands, but that is the total of the confederation and not a return for this battle. No number survives for the size of the Gepid coalition either; what can be matched to it in the archaeological record is the mass of socketed spearheads, lamellar armour fragments and horse harness recovered from fourth- and fifth-century burials in western Hungary. In time, the battle was decided in a single day; in distance, the Nedao valley lies about one hundred and fifty to two hundred kilometres from the Danube, and the Gepid kingdom built by Ardaric afterwards covered the country between the Tisza and the Danube, on the order of a hundred thousand square kilometres. Other datable events that can be checked: Attila reigned from 434 to 453, the letter of Leo I to Ardaric belongs to 455, the Huns under Dengizich rebelled against Rome and were defeated in 469 and 470, Rome settled a body of Huns in Pannonia in 476, Odoacer destroyed the Rugii who still held the middle Danube in 487, and the Gepid kingdom survived until around 568, when the Lombards and the Avars swept it away.
cause: 起因要分遠因與近因。遠因是草原帝國的結構：匈人帝國並非單一民族的國家，而是以匈奴王公為頂點、由被征服的日耳曼與羅馬屬部拼成的宗主與屬國關係，屬部要出兵、出馬、出貢，這種關係靠的是阿提拉個人的威望，一旦威望消失，帝國就沒有第二個黏合劑。近因是阿提拉之死與繼承危機：四五三年阿提拉死後，長子埃拉克接位，為維持帝國而先打壓不服的屬部，蓋皮德國王阿爾達里克趁勢率眾脫離；同時其他部族也各自求存，聯盟因此形成。關鍵的一步是埃拉克選擇用兵：他把剛剛安頓下來的帝國秩序視為可以靠刀兵收回的東西，直接推向蓋皮德人，逼得對方把所有仇怨湊成一支聯軍。還有一層被史家反覆強調的意義：這是羅馬帝國第一次不必自己出手，而是寫信去請一個外族替自己去打另一個外族。利奧一世的信裡稱阿爾達里克為王，承認他對自己境內的居民有完全的權力，等於確認了蓋皮德人從屬部變成主人的身分，而阿爾達里克的回信也正是本役在史料中留下名字的地方。
causeEn: The cause has to be split into a distant cause and an immediate one. The distant cause is the structure of a steppe empire: the Hunnic empire was not the state of a single people but a lordship-and-subjects arrangement built around a Hunnic prince and the conquered Germanic and Roman peoples, from whom the empire demanded troops, horses and tribute; such a relation rested on the personal prestige of Attila, and once that prestige was gone the empire had no second adhesive. The immediate cause was the death of Attila and the succession crisis: when Attila died in 453 the eldest son Ellac took over, and in order to hold the empire together he first struck at the disobedient subjects, so that Ardaric, king of the Gepids, led his people out of the empire; at the same time the other tribes were each trying to survive, and the alliance took shape. The decisive step was Ellac's choice of war: he treated the order that had just been established as something that could be taken back by force and drove it straight at the Gepids, forcing them to pool every grievance into a single coalition. There is also a layer of meaning that historians keep returning to: this was the first time the Roman empire did not have to fight by itself, but wrote a letter asking one foreign people to strike another foreign people on its behalf. Leo's letter calls Ardaric king and acknowledges his full authority over the people of his own land, which amounts to confirming the Gepids' change of status from subjects to masters, and Ardaric's reply is also the place where this battle is given a name in the sources.
impact: 短期看，這是匈人西進的終點：埃拉克陣亡，帝國的西翼崩落，匈人退回黑海北岸草原，此後數十年在多瑙河流域再也沒有成建制地出現；登吉奇四六九年背叛羅馬失敗被殺，四七六年一批匈人部眾被羅馬安置在潘諾尼亞，四七七年之後匈人甚至一度隨奧多亞克進入意大利，這條路把匈人從帝國的建設者變成羅馬可以收編的武力。中期看，蓋皮德人第一次以主人身分接管原屬匈人的多瑙河與蒂薩河流域，並且立刻被羅馬帝國當作屏障來經營：利奧一世之後的皇帝把潘諾尼亞的防務外包給蓋皮德王國，羅馬的錢、糧與武器沿多瑙河上溯，一支原本的屬部軍隊就這樣變成羅馬在北方的附庸王國。長期看，這場戰爭是草原帝國第一次因本部瓦解而崩盤的標本案例，後來匈人、柔然、突厥、蒙古的崩解幾乎都沿著同一條裂縫：主子一死，屬部即散，遊牧政權與被征服的定居民眾之間從來沒有真正焊在一起的制度。考古上，第四至第六世紀的匈牙利平原出現大批混合文化的墓葬，武器形制、馬具與陶器都帶著草原與歐亞西部兩種來源的痕跡，這些發現至今仍是重建這段歷史的主要依據。史學上更麻煩的是唯一來源約丹尼斯帶有明確的日耳曼系立場，他記下的這場勝利既是史料，也是宣傳，學者至今仍在辨別他哪些話可以當作史實。
impactEn: In the short run this was the end of the westward Hunnic drive: Ellac was killed, the western wing of the empire collapsed, the Huns withdrew to the steppe north of the Black Sea, and for decades they put no organised force back on the middle Danube; Dengizich betrayed Rome and was killed in 469, a body of Huns was settled by Rome in Pannonia in 476, and after 477 Huns even rode into Italy with Odoacer, a road that turned the Huns from the builders of an empire into a force Rome could enrol. In the medium run the Gepids for the first time took over the Danube and Tisza valleys of the former Hunnic sphere as masters, and were immediately treated by Rome as a buffer: under the emperors after Leo I the defence of Pannonia was subcontracted to the Gepid kingdom, Roman money, grain and arms moved up the Danube, and a former subject army turned into a client kingdom in the north. When the Ostrogoths entered Italy in 489 and later pushed the Gepids to the north-west in the 550s, the last Gepid kingdom was finally destroyed around 568 by the Lombards and the Avars, its last king Valamir withdrawing into the eastern empire. In the long run this war is the standard case of the first steppe empire to fall apart because its own core came apart, and the later dissolutions of the Huns, the Rouran, the Turks and the Mongols all ran along the same crack: when the master died the subjects scattered, because there had never been an institution that truly welded nomadic rule to the settled population. Archaeologically, the fourth- to sixth-century cemeteries of the Hungarian plain have yielded large numbers of burials of a mixed culture whose weapons, harness and pottery carry traces of both the steppe and of western Eurasia, and those finds remain the main evidence for reconstructing this period. More awkward for historians is the single source: Jordanes writes with a clear Germanic standpoint, so the victory he records is at once a source and a piece of propaganda, and scholars are still sorting out which of his statements can be taken as fact.
result: 結局是日耳曼聯盟完勝。埃拉克陣亡，匈人軍隊當場解體，一場持續數十里的追擊戰把匈人的營帳、馬群與戰利品全部易手；聯軍沒有攻下任何一座匈人城池，因為匈人本來就沒有可以攻的城池，他們的國土是草場與馬群，兵敗就等於失去一切能帶走的東西。戰後匈人勢力退出多瑙河中游，向黑海北岸與多瑙河下游收縮，逐漸退回草原；被阿提拉壓制了二十年的蓋皮德人則在原匈人疆域上建起自己的王國，阿爾達里克被推為共主，約丹尼斯宣稱他因此取得了西徐亞之王的稱號，蓋皮德人從此以匈人繼承者的身分面對草原世界。對羅馬而言，這是一筆意外收穫：不用羅馬兵，帝國得到一個新的北方屏障；對日耳曼世界而言，這是一個樣板：屬部可以用自己的兵推翻草原主子，並且靠勝仗取得王號、國土與羅馬的承認。戰役真正的尾聲發生在戰後數十年：匈人西來的路線改由柔然與阿伏爾人接手，蓋皮德王國在五六八年前後覆亡，而那支亞述長矛的影子，則從九百年前一路傳到中世紀的長矛陣裡，再傳到近代的騎槍與刺刀，仍然沒有斷。
resultEn: The outcome was a complete victory for the Germanic alliance. Ellac was killed, the Hunnic army dissolved on the spot, and a pursuit of many miles left the Huns' tents, horse herds and plunder entirely in the other side's hands; the alliance took no Hunnic city, because the Huns had no cities to take, their country being pasture and horses, so a lost battle meant losing everything that could be carried away. Afterwards Hunnic power withdrew from the middle Danube, contracting towards the Black Sea coast and the lower Danube and gradually returning to the steppe; the Gepids, oppressed for twenty years by Attila, built a kingdom of their own over the former Hunnic territory, Ardaric was acknowledged as their joint leader, and Jordanes claims that he thereby took the title of king of the Scythians, so that the Gepids henceforth faced the steppe world as the heirs of the Huns. For Rome this was a windfall: no Roman soldiers, and a new northern shield; for the Germanic world it was a model: subject peoples could use their own troops to overthrow their steppe overlord and, on the strength of the victory, obtain a royal title, a territory and Roman recognition. The real epilogue came decades later: the road west taken by the Huns was taken up by the Rouran and the Avars, the Gepid kingdom ended around 568, and the shadow of the Assyrian spear, from nine centuries before, ran on into the medieval pike line and from there into the lance and the bayonet, and was never broken.
